land.text: Chengdu and the Yi Province core, which Li Xiong took from Luo Shang in 304

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Western Jin' as predecessor; dates 303 or 304 to 347.

land.text: Chengdu and the Sichuan basin, where 'Huan Wen reached Chengdu and forced Li Shi to surrender' in 347

successors.note: The Eastern Jin is the infobox's successor; it is the later half of the western-jin dossier (Cliopatria's Western Jin row runs to 425).

capitals.name: Chengdu
capitals.note: Chengdu is the only capital named; 'Li Xiong ousted Luo Shang from Chengdu, where he declared himself the King of Chengdu'.

rulers.name: Li Xiong (Taizong, 'Wu')
rulers.note: Ruler table gives 303-334 (it starts the line at Li Te's 303 rebellion and Li Liu); the text and the Li Xiong page date his rule from 304. Li Te (d. 303) and Li Liu (303) precede the state's 304 start.

rulers.name: Li Ban
rulers.note: Killed shortly after taking the throne.

rulers.name: Li Qi
rulers.note: Forced to abdicate by Li Shou in 338.

rulers.name: Li Shi
rulers.note: Surrendered to Huan Wen in 347; died at Jiankang in 361.

correction.text: Cheng-Han's core in 304-310: the Sichuan basin around Chengdu, without Chongqing (Ba Commandery, where Luo Shang held out until 310), Hanzhong (Cheng only from 314) and the Yunnan and Guizhou corners of Ning Province (taken in 333); drawn from 304, the year Li Xiong 'captured Chengdu'

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's shape (468,000 km2 by the gazetteer's cells, 452,000 in the table) already contains about 43,000 km2 of Yunnan and 7,600 of Guizhou, 31,000 of Chongqing and 20,000 of Hanzhong, and starts in 306. The Li Xiong page: 'In c.February 304, Li Xiong captured Chengdu'; he 'made no serious attempts to capture Jin's Ning Province' (footnote: 333, Li Shou); the Cheng-Han page: after 304 'Luo Shang commanded from Ba Commandery (present-day Chongqing)' until 310, and Hanzhong came in 314. The corrected core is 366,000 km2. The infobox has no area; its territory 'modern-day Sichuan Province' (the gazetteer's Sichuan and Chongqing together are 589,000 km2) is the same order.

correction.text: Yi Province with Chongqing from 310 ('Cheng dispatched [the Jin forces] and consolidated their rule'), without Hanzhong until 314 and without Ning Province's Yunnan and Guizhou until 333; the ledger adds Hanzhong (314) and Ning (333) to this baseline

keyframe_review.note: Years 311-337 hold three shapes in one: the Cliopatria 311 outline already holds Ning Province, which the Li Xiong page (footnote) has Li Shou capturing in 333, and Hanzhong, which 'rebelling refugees ... surrendered ... to Cheng' in 314. Corrected baseline 348,000 km2; the full 468,000 km2 holds from 333.

correction.text: unchanged shape, drawn through 347 instead of 346: 'In 347, Huan Wen reached Chengdu and forced Li Shi to surrender, ending the dynasty'; the state is renamed Han in 338

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria ends in 346, one year early; the page's infobox says 'disestablished 347'. The Li Xiong page notes that Liang Province (梁州, which the page places in modern southern Shaanxi, i.e. the Hanzhong country, and warns is not Liangzhou 涼州 in Gansu) 'reverted several times between Jin and Cheng-Han rule' during Li Xiong's reign (304-334); the Hanzhong piece of the Cliopatria shape is therefore Cheng's from 314 only intermittently, and no page opened dates the reversals. [Reviewer ea-03-b: corrected from 'Liang Province (Gansu)'.]

ledger.note: 304: Li Xiong takes Chengdu and founds the Cheng. 'In c.February 304, Li Xiong captured Chengdu, the capital of Yi Province, forcing Luo Shang to flee'; he declared himself Prince of Chengdu in November or December, and the Cheng-Han page: 'Most historians date the dynasty's start to this event' (infobox: 303 or 304). Month 2 is kept in identity.start; the event carries no month so that the same-year contest event sorts after it.

region.text: Ba Commandery (present-day Chongqing), from which Luo Shang 'continued to threaten Cheng'

ledger.note: 304: Luo Shang holds out in Ba. 'After 304, Luo Shang commanded from Ba Commandery (present-day Chongqing) and continued to threaten Cheng.' Luo Shang's attack on the refugees began Li Te's rebellion in 301 and the Jin were fighting in Yi Province from then.
306: Li Xiong becomes emperor. 'In c.July 306, he declared himself emperor and named his empire "Cheng" (成)': the Prince of Chengdu becomes the Cheng empire; same state, same colour.
310: Luo Shang dies and Yi Province is Cheng's. 'Luo Shang died. Jin forces fell into disarray, allowing Cheng to dispatch them and consolidate their rule.'

region.text: Ba Commandery, present-day Chongqing, where Luo Shang had held out

ledger.note: 310: Chongqing comes under the Cheng. The page says the Jin forces were dispatched and Cheng 'consolidate[d] their rule' after Luo Shang's death in 310; the Li Xiong page says Li Xiong was 'occupying all of Yi Province'. The region is my reading (Ba Commandery = Chongqing, per the page).
314: Hanzhong goes to the Cheng. 'A group of rebelling refugees in Hanzhong surrendered the region to Cheng.'

region.text: Ning Province, the Yunnan and Guizhou corner that Cliopatria's shape holds

ledger.note: 333: Li Shou takes Ning Province. The Li Xiong page, in a footnote: Li Xiong 'made no serious attempts to capture Jin's Ning Province'; 'in 333 his cousin Li Shou captured it'. The page names Ning Province (Yunnan and Guizhou); how much of it Cheng held is the researcher's reading of Cliopatria's shape.
338: the Cheng becomes the Han. 'Li Shou forced Li Qi to abdicate and renamed the state Han'; same state, same colour (the page's Cheng-Han).

region.text: the Cheng-Han realm, Chengdu and the Sichuan basin

ledger.note: 346: Huan Wen sets out. 'Huan Wen set off to conquer Han'.
347: Huan Wen takes Chengdu. 'Huan Wen reached Chengdu and forced Li Shi to surrender, ending the dynasty.'

region.text: Chengdu and the Sichuan basin, 'the Eastern Jin' succeeding the Han

ledger.note: 347: the Cheng-Han ends. Li Shi surrenders to Huan Wen; he 'died in Jiankang, the Eastern Jin capital' in 361. Sichuan returns to the Jin.

wars.name: Cheng-Jin war for Yi Province

zones.text: Yi Province: Chengdu and Ba Commandery

wars.outcome: Li Te's rebellion (301) and the death of Luo Shang (310) leave Yi Province to the Cheng; Luo Shang's Jin forces held Ba Commandery after 304.
wars.note: Cheng-Han starts in 304 (Li Xiong at Chengdu); 301-303 are Li Te's rebellion.

wars.name: Eastern Jin conquest of Cheng-Han (Huan Wen)
wars.outcome: Huan Wen set off in 346 and reached Chengdu in 347; Li Shi surrendered and the dynasty ended.

certainty.note: Commandery and province frontiers in the Sichuan basin and its mountain rim; no page opened gives a treaty or survey line. The Yunnan and Guizhou edge (Ning Province) and Hanzhong are the softest.

sources.title: Cheng-Han
sources.note: Infobox (303 or 304 to 347), Chengdu, Ba Commandery, 310, 314, 338, 346-347, ruler table.

sources.title: Li Xiong
sources.note: 304 capture of Chengdu, 306 emperor, Yi Province occupied, Ning Province taken in 333 (footnote), Liang Province reverted several times.

notes:
Cliopatria rows: 'Cheng Han', 3 shapes, 306..346, all reviewed; the three outlines are the same 452,000 km2 (a single shape in practice), so the corrections subtract the Yunnan, Guizhou, Chongqing and Hanzhong pieces for the years the two pages show Cheng did not hold them, and the ledger adds them back (310 Chongqing, 314 Hanzhong, 333 Ning). Cliopatria starts 306 and ends 346; the pages give 304 (Li Xiong at Chengdu) and 347 (Li Shi's surrender).
Unsettled: (1) the extent of Ning Province under Cheng after 333 is unknown (footnote on the Li Xiong page only); (2) Liang Province (梁州, southern Shaanxi, i.e. Hanzhong, per the Li Xiong page; not Liangzhou in Gansu): 'reverted several times between Jin and Cheng-Han rule' with no dates, so the Hanzhong gain of 314 held only intermittently to 334; (3) the Huan Wen page was not opened (budget 1-2 pages), so the 346 campaign is dated from the Cheng-Han page's year only; (4) the Cheng-Han page has Li Xiong from 303 in the ruler table and 304 in the text; (5) the infobox gives no area.
Counterpart: 'western-jin' stands for both the Western and the Eastern Jin (one dossier); the Western Jin dossier already has the matching losses (304, 314, 347) and the 301-310 contest.
Wikidata Q1069905 is Cliopatria's. Names for the gazetteer: none new (Chongqing, Yunnan, Guizhou admin1; Hanzhong and Chengdu places).
